extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, journalism students, and practitioners interested in news values and newsworthiness
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly review and empirical test of established news-value taxonomies (Galtung & Ruge; Harcup & O'Neill) to assess whether and how news values have changed in the digital age, including the effects of social media and shareability. The paper includes a literature review and a fresh content analysis of UK media and proposes an updated list of contemporary news values.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values
rubrics_metrics.description: The deceptively simple question 'What is news?' — examines news values within mainstream journalism and considers the extent to which news values may be changing since earlier landmark studies were undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reviews literature and conducts a fresh content analysis of UK media to assess the continuing relevance of established news values; it frames the enquiry as foundational to understanding selection and production decisions in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harcup & O'Neill (2001) revised list of news values
rubrics_metrics.description: Harcup and O'Neill's widely-cited 2001 updating of Galtung and Ruge's influential 1965 taxonomy of news values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the starting point for the current study; the 2001 list was itself an empirical test of Galtung & Ruge and is being re-examined here to see whether its components remain relevant in contemporary media contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galtung & Ruge (1965) taxonomy of news values
rubrics_metrics.description: Galtung and Ruge's influential 1965 taxonomy of news values, an earlier landmark framework for identifying what makes events newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as the foundational taxonomy against which later updates (including Harcup & O'Neill 2001) and current reassessments are measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of news values in the digital age (social media and shareability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the extent to which news values may be changing given the challenges (and opportunities) faced by journalism today, including the emergence of social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study specifically examines how aspects like shareability driven by social media platforms may alter which items are selected as news; this theme informs both the literature review and empirical content analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical content analysis of news values
rubrics_metrics.description: A fresh content analysis of news values within a range of UK media conducted 15 years on from the last study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test the applicability and visibility of the listed news values in current published news; contextualised by a review of recent literature to interpret observed changes or continuities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised and updated set of contemporary news values
rubrics_metrics.description: The article concludes by suggesting a revised and updated set of contemporary news values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed updated taxonomy is offered as a synthesis of literature review and empirical findings, with the authors acknowledging that 'no taxonomy can ever explain everything.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection (keyword listed in the article metadata) — the process and criteria by which news items are chosen for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied focus of the study: investigating which values influence editorial selection in modern newsrooms and digital platforms.
